source: ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted **on the worker thread**. A closure connected to it is invoked there. Touching a widget from it is undefined behaviour. The only safe thing a slot on that signal may do is re-emit a ``Signal`` whose receiver is a bound method of a GUI-thread object -- Qt then queues the call onto the GUI thread.
context: ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted **on the background execution unit**. A closure connected to it is invoked there. Touching a widget from it is undefined behaviour. The only safe thing a slot on that signal may do is re-emit a ``Signal`` whose receiver is a bound method of a main GUI execution path object -- Qt then schedules the call onto the main GUI execution path.

semantic_findings: The old er geymt means stored and did not describe signal emission. The replacement er sent means sent/emitted.
The revised wording explicitly places emission and the connected closure on the worker thread.
Widget access from that worker-thread callback remains undefined behavior, rather than an unspecified stored-state claim.
The safe relay re-emits literal Signal to a bound method of a GUI-thread object.
The final sentence accurately describes Qt queuing the call for execution on the GUI thread.
source_readback: PipelineWorker.run emits finished(False) on pre-start cancellation and finished(ok) in its final cleanup.
bridge.make_thread moves the worker to the thread and connects thread.started to worker.run.
JobRunner.submit connects worker.finished to the closure calling _relay.
JobRunner._relay emits _settled; the runner connects _settled to its bound _on_settled method.
